mg_a_carving_for_danny.description: I've carved a wee plank for Danny Kowalczyk, the Wakened who keeps trying to fall asleep and wake up back home in Buffalo. Danny's never carved anything for the wall, and I think he might, if somebody else starts it for him. It's his house, as near as I could get it from what he's told me, with a porch, two wee boys on the steps and a dog I've made up. Danny's usually by the dream cots outside the infirmary. Take it over to him for me.
mg_a_carving_for_danny.accept_text: Don't tell him it's from me until he's had a good look at it.

mg_a_doctor_and_a_keeper.description: I've copied out what the sleepers said, line by line, with the languages beside them. I've never asked Keeper Remulos for anything before, but I think he needs to see this, and I think he might listen to someone who isn't me. He's always been kind to us, and he's always treated us like patients. Remulos is under his tree on the north-west point, so take this to him at his shrine. Tell him it's from the doctor, not from one of the sleepers.
mg_a_doctor_and_a_keeper.accept_text: Let him read it all the way through before you say anything.

mg_a_lantern_for_the_longhouse.description: Keeper Remulos has told me about Ingrid Sandvik's transcript, and I've decided the Circle owes the Wakened more than politeness. I'm sending them a moon lantern lit from the great moonwell, the same kind that hangs over every druid's door in Nighthaven. Take it to Dr. Sandvik at the longhouse, and hang it over the door if she'll let you. It means the Wakened are welcome in any druid's house in Kalimdor, and that we'd like to be welcome in theirs. We should have done it three years ago.
mg_a_lantern_for_the_longhouse.accept_text: Carry it by the base, not the ring. The flame doesn't like being swung.

mg_bloodvenom.description: I've kept Nighthaven's great moonwell for longer than most of Kalimdor has had names. I believe the water under Felwood and the water under Moonglade are the same water, and I want to know how much of the Bloodvenom has found its way up the mountain. The Seepage Oozes at Bloodvenom Falls, in North Felwood, are the poison given a body. Bring me what's inside them, sealed in wax, and don't let it touch your skin. I'll set it beside a cup of moonwell water and see what each of them does.
mg_bloodvenom.accept_text: Seal it twice if you can. Once never seems to be enough with that stuff.

mg_iron_from_nothing.description: The wall of last memories has worn out every chisel we own. I want proper steel ones, and our new forge can make them, if somebody brings the ore. The Circle won't have mining in the glade, so it has to come from outside. Thorium's in the hard country, the Plaguelands, Azshara's mountains and the passes up here. Bring me the ore and Tomas Ribeiro will smelt it, because he sold hammers in Porto for nineteen years and now he wants to make one.
mg_iron_from_nothing.accept_text: Bring a bit extra if you can. Tomas will ruin the first batch, and he knows it.

mg_moonwell_water_for_the_totems.description: I've decided to raise one of the totems we carried out of Thunder Bluff. I'll raise only one, for the ones we carried and not the ones we left. Before it goes up it has to be washed, and I want the water from Nighthaven's great moonwell, with Aedris Silverbrook's blessing. Aedris has already filled the flask, put it in my hands, and then taken it back and said someone else should carry it. I think she means it shouldn't be one of us, so take it from her and bring it here.
mg_moonwell_water_for_the_totems.accept_text: Walk it slowly. I'd like the water to arrive as calm as it left.

mg_satyrs_in_the_green.description: Felwood was the Circle's forest before the Legion poisoned it, and the satyrs of the Jadefire are still there, still spreading the rot. I send the Circle's help out to the sick lands, and I'd like to send you. The Jadefire Felsworn and the Jadefire Tricksters run in North Felwood, round the Jadefire glens. The Felsworn are the ones spreading the fel, and the Tricksters are the ones making sure nobody stops them. Thin them both out for me.
mg_satyrs_in_the_green.accept_text: Don't let the Tricksters get behind you. That's where they do their worst.

mg_seedlings_for_the_sanctuary.description: I grow seedlings from the glade's oldest trees, and the Emerald Reclamation in Felwood has asked for them. They want to plant them where the fel has been burned away. Moonglade's soil is the cleanest in Kalimdor, and the Sanctuary needs every bit of it. I've packed a tray, and it needs carrying carefully. Will you take it down for me?
mg_seedlings_for_the_sanctuary.accept_text: Fly down to the Emerald Sanctuary in South Felwood and give the tray to Arch Druid Aelyra Moonbough. Keep them away from Felwood's water.

mg_something_to_grow.description: My grandmother grew chillies on a balcony in Chengdu, and I plant things in the Wakened's gardens because it's how I know where I am. The druids grow everything here without any help from me. I want something that's mine. I'd like a bed of Golden Sansam, which grows wild in the high places and nowhere in the glade. If you bring me some with the roots on, I'll do the rest.
mg_something_to_grow.accept_text: Golden Sansam grows in Felwood, Azshara and the high passes. Pick it with the roots on, and wrap it in damp moss.

mg_ten_thousand_years_of_horns.description: The Circle has kept a count of satyrs since the War of the Ancients, horn by horn. I've taken over the counting since I came, partly because the night elves asked and partly because it gives a tauren something to do with his hands. The Legash Satyrs hold the old ruins in Central Azshara, round the Legash encampment. Bring me their horns, and I'll add them to the count. Then I'll tell the night elves, and they'll pretend they're not impressed.
mg_ten_thousand_years_of_horns.accept_text: Keep them in a sack, not tied to your belt. Satyr horn rattles, and the Legash listen.

mg_the_black_gate.description: Behind the Black Gate of Jaedenar, the Shadow Council keeps a demon chained. Zar'gothrax the Unbound has been pulling at those chains since the worlds came together. The Circle has felt every pull in the roots of the glade, and so have I. I want the demon dead. I've waited three years for someone who could do it.
mg_the_black_gate.accept_text: Jaedenar's in the north-west of North Felwood, behind the Black Gate. Zar'gothrax is at the very bottom, so take friends you trust.

mg_the_first_morning.description: When the worlds came together, the transplants who came through near Moonglade arrived asleep. I woke up on the grass by the lake with a druid standing over me. I spent twenty years in Trondheim studying sleep, what the brain does at night and why it dreams, and I'd have told you I knew everything about it from the outside. There are two places here that tell the rest of it: the wall where the Wakened carve their last memories, and the cots outside the infirmary where the ones who don't wake are kept. Go and read the wall, then sit for a while by the cots, and come back and tell me which of them frightened you more.
mg_the_first_morning.accept_text: Read the planks slowly. Every one of them took somebody a long time to carve.

mg_the_fish_are_turning.description: I've fished Lake Elune'ara my whole life, and the fish have started turning toward the island at night. All of them turn, the way a field of flowers turns to the sun. My mother fished this lake, and her mother before her, and neither of them ever saw it. I want someone else to see it, so I know I'm not imagining it. The falls are where the water's clearest.
mg_the_fish_are_turning.accept_text: The Falls of Elune'ara come down on the north shore. Stand where the spray settles and look into the water.

mg_the_last_thing_you_remember.description: I started the wall of last memories with my mother's kitchen on the Isle of Lewis. Every new Wakened carves a plank now, and I'm out of wood, because the Circle won't let anyone cut a living tree in the glade. I've found a way round it that the druids have agreed to, just about. The Warpwood Treants in North Felwood were trees once, before the fel got into them, and under the bark the heartwood's still sound. Put them out of their misery and bring me the heartwood, because the Circle says that's kinder than leaving them, and I'd like to think they're right.
mg_the_last_thing_you_remember.accept_text: Bring me the straight pieces if you can. A crooked plank fights the chisel the whole way.

mg_the_man_who_wants_to_sleep.description: I was asleep in Buffalo when the worlds came together, and I woke up here. I think if I fall asleep the right way, in the right place, I'll wake up back there with my wife and my boys. Ingrid says it doesn't work like that, and Adaeze says I'm going to hurt myself, and maybe they're right. Tonight I want to try it on the north shore, where the moonlight lies on the water, and I don't want to do it alone. Come and sit with me there, and if I don't wake up in the morning, you can tell them they were wrong.
mg_the_man_who_wants_to_sleep.accept_text: Bring a blanket if you've got one. It gets cold by the water after midnight.

mg_the_night_watch.description: The Wakened keep a watch every night, because somebody ought to be awake in a valley full of sleepers. I can't sleep, so I took the rota over, and tonight I'm short a watchman. The round takes in the three places in Moonglade we don't like to leave alone in the dark. It's the Dreaming Arch in the north woods first, then down the west shore to the Barrow Dens' door, then all the way round to the end of the pier in Nighthaven. You don't have to do anything at any of them, so just look, and remember what you saw.
mg_the_night_watch.accept_text: Stop at the end of the pier for a minute before you come back. That's the best part of the watch.

mg_the_ones_who_dont_wake.description: Not every transplant who arrived asleep in Moonglade woke up. I visit the ones who didn't, in the Barrow Dens beside the druids, and lately their sleep has turned restless. A draught of Dreamfoil eases a dreamer's sleep without waking them, and the glade doesn't grow it. It grows in the high wild places, in Felwood and Azshara and the passes, so bring me the leaves fresh and I'll steep them tonight. I can't wake them, but I can make sure they're not frightened while they sleep.
mg_the_ones_who_dont_wake.accept_text: Wrap the leaves in something damp. Dry Dreamfoil makes a bitter draught.

mg_the_rot_under_the_hold.description: The Timbermaw took my people in for a night on their way up the mountain, when the tauren had nowhere else to go. Now the Timbermaw have a rot of their own under Timbermaw Hold in Azshara, and I haven't forgotten the debt. Under the Hold there's the Rotroot Deeps, and at the bottom of it waits Xavras the Gloomtender, the satyr growing the fel into the Hold's own roots. Go through the deep gate in the Hold's basin, and take friends with you. The Timbermaw will thank you, and so will I.
mg_the_rot_under_the_hold.accept_text: The roots will grab at you down there. Cut them before they close.

mg_the_same_dream.description: I keep a book for my guests to write in, and for the last month half of them have written down the same dream. It's a door under water, and a stair going down. These are people who've never met, writing the same thing in their own words, and it's all in the back half of the book. I want Dr. Sandvik to see it, because she's the only one in the glade who collects dreams on purpose. Take it round the lake to her for me.
mg_the_same_dream.accept_text: Don't read it on the road, please. They wrote in it for me, not for strangers.

mg_the_thunder_bluff_road.description: I flew the Thunder Bluff road for twenty years before it fell. Elder Longtread at Camp Taurajo keeps the seat for Cairne Bloodhoof, and I've never been able to bring myself to fly him the list of who reached Moonglade. Archdruid Hamuul has written it out, every name. Someone has to carry it, and I can't. Will you take it to him for me?
mg_the_thunder_bluff_road.accept_text: Camp Taurajo's in the Southern Barrens. Give Longtread the list, and tell him we looked, and that's everyone.

mg_the_totems_on_our_backs.description: When Thunder Bluff fell, those of us who reached Moonglade carried our lodges' totems up the mountain on our backs. I've kept them laid down ever since. The survivors built a memorial, and we've argued about it for three years. I'd like someone who wasn't there to stand at it and tell me what it looks like to a stranger. Tell me honestly whether it looks like a grave or a promise.
mg_the_totems_on_our_backs.accept_text: The memorial's a short walk south-east of here, by the lodges, a cairn with feathers on it. Look at it properly, then come back.

mg_the_way_up.description: The Moonglade passage past my spring was buried for three years, and the druids dug it out from their side. I've filled a jar from my spring for the Circle, so they'll know what the mountain's water tastes of down here. Take it up the Moonglade passage, past the boulders they rolled aside, and out into the glade. Give the jar to Rabine Saturna in Nighthaven. Tell him the water still tastes of Felwood, and that I'm sorry for it.
mg_the_way_up.accept_text: Hold it upright on the climb. The stopper's old, and I'd hate for it to arrive half empty.

mg_the_well_runs_over.description: Every night the great moonwell runs over by a finger's width, and every morning it's settled again. I've been writing down the times, and they match something on the lake. I can't watch both at once. I want someone at the end of Nighthaven's pier to watch the island in the middle of the lake while I watch the well. When the well rises, I'll know, and I think you'll know too, so come back and tell me what you saw.
mg_the_well_runs_over.accept_text: Don't take your eyes off the island, even when it seems like nothing is happening.

mg_waking_badly.description: Some of the Wakened still wake badly, sitting up in the dark not knowing which world they're in. I've found that the soft light of a wisp calms them faster than anything I could have given them in Lagos. The Moonlit Wisps drift through South Felwood, round the Emerald Sanctuary, and when they fade their light stays behind for a while. Catch it in your hands and bring it to me. I'll hang it over the cots, and nobody will wake up in the dark again.
mg_waking_badly.accept_text: Cup it close and walk steady. It dims if you jostle it.

mg_warm_stones.description: The Dreaming Arch in the north woods has stood cold for ten thousand years. Now its stones are warm at night, and the flowers round it bloom only when they are. I sit with it every night, and I'd like a second pair of eyes I can trust. It's up the path into the north woods, behind the Shrine, so go after dark and put your hands flat on the stones and hold them there. Tell me if they feel warm like a hearth, or warm like something alive.
mg_warm_stones.accept_text: Don't pick the flowers. They close if anyone touches them, and they're slow to open again.

mg_welcome_to_nighthaven.description: The great moonwell's in the square, a few steps north of here. Look into it for a while. Then follow the shore road round to the west side, where the Wakened live, and give Dr. Sandvik this letter. She'll explain them better than I can.
mg_welcome_to_nighthaven.accept_text: Take your time at the well. Nobody in Nighthaven will hurry you.

mg_what_dies_in_deadwind.description: I can walk the Emerald Dream to almost anywhere in Azeroth. Since the worlds came together there's one place I can't reach, and that's Deadwind Pass. I want to know what's happening to the living things there. The deer of the pass will tell me, if you bring me what's left of them. The bone remembers what the animal dreamed, and I'll read it.
mg_what_dies_in_deadwind.accept_text: The Dissolving Stags wander Deadwind West, coming apart a little more every day. Bring me their antlers.

mg_what_is_waking.description: The sleepers answer someone, the arch is warm, the well runs over when the island lights, and strangers dream of a stair under the water. I've listened to all of it, and now I mean to walk into the Dream and look. I want you at my shrine while I'm gone. Stand by the moonwell under my tree, and if I don't come back by morning, don't wake me, whatever the druids tell you. Go to Ingrid Sandvik instead, because she'll know better than they will how to bring somebody back.
mg_what_is_waking.accept_text: Sit where you can see my face. If anything changes, I'd like you to be the first to notice.

mg_what_the_sleepers_say.description: The druids and the Wakened who sleep in the Barrow Dens have started talking in their sleep. I want someone to sit outside the door and write down what they say, because the wardens won't, and the Circle has asked me not to go myself. The Barrow Dens are south of here, in the hills, and Warden Taerenas will let you sit by the door if you don't touch it. Write down everything, even the words you don't understand, and those most of all. I've heard that some of it isn't in any language they speak here.
mg_what_the_sleepers_say.accept_text: Take plenty of ink. You won't want to stop once they start.

mg_who_are_they_talking_to.description: I guard the Barrow Dens' door, and I've heard the sleepers inside answering someone. They aren't talking to each other, I'm sure of it. They're talking to someone else. I need a witness who isn't a warden, because the Circle will say a warden was only frightened. Stand at the door with me and listen, nothing more.
mg_who_are_they_talking_to.accept_text: Don't touch the thorns. If you hear it, you'll know, because it's the only voice in there that doesn't sound asleep.
